title.raw: 卷十九 志第九 禮樂九 Volume 19 Treatises 9: Rites and Music 9

sentences.zh: 嘉禮三

translations.literal: Auspicious Rites Three
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious Rites III

sentences.zh: 皇帝元正、冬至受群臣朝賀而會

translations.literal: The emperor on New Year's Day and the winter solstice receives the court's congratulatory audience and holds a feast.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice the emperor receives the ministers' congratulations and holds a court feast.

sentences.zh: 皇帝元正、冬至受群臣朝賀而會。

translations.literal: The emperor on New Year's Day and the winter solstice receives the court's congratulatory audience and holds a feast.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice the emperor receives the ministers' congratulations and holds a court feast.

sentences.zh: 前一日，尚舍設禦幄於太極殿，有司設群官客使等次於東西朝堂，展縣，置桉，陳車輿，又設解劍席於縣西北橫街之南。

translations.literal: On the previous day the Imperial Household Service set the imperial canopy in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the relevant offices set ranks for officials, envoys, and guests in the eastern and western audience halls, suspended the bells, set tables, arrayed carriages, and also set sword-removal mats south of the transverse street northwest of the bells.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the Imperial Household Service erected the imperial enclosure in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; officials arranged seating in the east and west audience halls, hung bells, set tables, lined up carriages, and placed sword-removal mats south of the transverse street northwest of the bell frame.

sentences.zh: 文官三品以上位於橫街之南，道東；

translations.literal: Civil officials of the third rank and above stood south of the transverse street, east of the roadway;
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank civil officials and above stood south of the transverse street, east of the lane;

sentences.zh: 褒聖侯位於三品之下，介公、酅公位於道西；

translations.literal: the Marquis Who Honors the Sage stood below the third rank; the Duke of Jie and the Duke of Xi stood west of the roadway;
translations.idiomatic: the Marquis Who Honors the Sage stood below third rank; the Duke of Jie and the Duke of Xi stood west of the lane;

sentences.zh: 武官三品以上位於介公之西，少南；

translations.literal: military officials of the third rank and above stood west of the Duke of Jie, slightly to the south;
translations.idiomatic: third-rank military officials and above stood west of the Duke of Jie, slightly south;

sentences.zh: 文官四品、五品位於縣東，六品以下位於橫街之南。

translations.literal: civil officials of the fourth and fifth ranks stood east of the bells; those of the sixth rank and below stood south of the transverse street.
translations.idiomatic: fourth- and fifth-rank civil officials stood east of the bells; sixth rank and below stood south of the transverse street.

sentences.zh: 又設諸州朝集使位：都督、刺史三品以上位於文、武官三品之東、西，四品以下分方位于文、武官當品之下。

translations.literal: Ranks were also set for provincial assembly envoys: governors and prefects of the third rank and above stood east and west of the third-rank civil and military officials; those of the fourth rank and below were placed by direction below officials of the corresponding rank.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial assembly envoys were placed likewise: third-rank governors and prefects flanked the third-rank civil and military lines; fourth rank and below were arrayed by region under peers of their grade.

sentences.zh: 諸州使人又於朝集使之下，諸親於四品、五品之南。

translations.literal: Provincial envoys stood again below the assembly envoys; imperial kinsmen stood south of the fourth- and fifth-rank officials.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial delegates stood below the assembly envoys; imperial relatives south of the fourth- and fifth-rank ranks.

sentences.zh: 設諸蕃方客位：三等以上，東方、南方在東方朝集使之東，西方、北方在西方朝集使之西，每國異位重行，北面；

translations.literal: Ranks for foreign guests were set: those of the third grade and above—eastern and southern realms east of the eastern assembly envoys, western and northern realms west of the western assembly envoys, each state in a separate row facing north;
translations.idiomatic: Foreign guests were placed by grade: third rank and above from the east and south stood east of the eastern envoys, those from the west and north west of the western envoys, each state in its own row facing north;

sentences.zh: 四等以下，分方位於朝集使六品之下。

translations.literal: those of the fourth grade and below were placed by direction below the sixth-rank assembly envoys.
translations.idiomatic: fourth rank and below were positioned by region below sixth-rank assembly envoys.

sentences.zh: 又設門外位：文官于東朝堂，介公、酅公在西朝堂之前，武官在介公之南，少退，每等異位重行；

translations.literal: Ranks outside the gate were also set: civil officials in the eastern audience hall; the Duke of Jie and the Duke of Xi before the western audience hall; military officials south of the Duke of Jie, slightly withdrawn, each grade in a separate row;
translations.idiomatic: Outside the gate, civil officials stood in the eastern hall; the Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi before the western hall; military officials south of the Duke of Jie, slightly back, each grade in its own row;

sentences.zh: 諸親位於文、武官四品、五品之南；

translations.literal: imperial kinsmen stood south of the fourth- and fifth-rank civil and military officials;
translations.idiomatic: imperial kin stood south of the fourth- and fifth-rank civil and military lines;

sentences.zh: 諸州朝集使，東方、南方在宗親之南，使人分方於朝集使之下；

translations.literal: provincial assembly envoys from the east and south stood south of the imperial clansmen, envoys placed by direction below the assembly envoys;
translations.idiomatic: eastern and southern assembly envoys stood south of the clansmen, with provincial delegates below them by region;

sentences.zh: 諸方客，東方、南方在東方朝集使之南，西方、北方在西方朝集使之南，每國異位重行。

translations.literal: foreign guests from the east and south stood south of the eastern assembly envoys, those from the west and north south of the western assembly envoys, each state in a separate row.
translations.idiomatic: eastern and southern guests stood south of the eastern envoys, western and northern guests south of the western envoys, each state in its own row.

sentences.zh: 其日，將士填諸街，勒所部列黃麾大仗屯門及陳於殿庭，群官就次。

translations.literal: On that day soldiers filled the streets; commanders arrayed their units, posted yellow-banner great halberds at the gates and in the hall court, and officials took their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: That day troops lined the streets; commanders formed their detachments, posted yellow-banner great halberds at gates and in the hall court, and officials took station.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏「請中嚴」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized on the board: "Request inner vigilance."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant submitted on the board: "Request inner vigilance."

sentences.zh: 諸侍衛之官詣閣奉迎，吏部兵部主客戶部贊群官、客使俱出次，通事舍人各引就朝堂前位，引四品以下及諸親、客等應先置者入就位。

translations.literal: Guards went to the pavilion to welcome; the Ministries of Personnel, War, Receptions, and Revenue ushered officials and envoys from their ranks; Protocol Aides each led them to positions before the audience hall, and led fourth rank and below, kinsmen, guests, and others who should enter first to their places.
translations.idiomatic: Guard officers went to the pavilion to receive the emperor; Personnel, War, Receptions, and Revenue directors ushered officials and envoys from their stations; Protocol Aides led each group to the audience-hall positions and brought in fourth rank and below, kin, guests, and others who were to enter first.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized on the board: "The outer rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported on the board: "Outer preparations complete."

sentences.zh: 皇帝服袞冕，冬至則服通天冠、絳紗袍，禦輿出自西房，即御座南向坐。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the coronation robe and cap; on the winter solstice he wore the open-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, rode the imperial carriage out from the western chamber, and took the throne facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore full ceremonial dress; on the winter solstice he wore the open-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, came out from the west chamber by imperial carriage, and took the throne facing south.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎奉寶置於前，公、王以下及諸客使等以次入就位。

translations.literal: The Talisman-and-Seal Officer presented the seals before him; dukes, princes, and below and all envoys and guests entered in order to their places.
translations.idiomatic: The Talisman-and-Seal Officer set the seals before him; dukes, princes, and below, with all envoys and guests, entered in sequence to their stations.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」贊者承傳，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " The announcers relayed it; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The announcers passed the word; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 上公一人詣西階席，脫舄，跪，解劍置於席，升，當御座前，北面跪賀，稱：「某官臣某言：元正首祚，景福惟新，伏惟開元神武皇帝陛下與天同休。

translations.literal: One senior duke went to the mat on the western steps, removed his shoes, knelt, removed his sword and set it on the mat, ascended, and before the throne knelt northward to offer congratulations, saying: "Such-and-such an official, your servant So-and-so, says: On the first day of the year, the year's fortune begins anew; may Your Majesty the Kaiyuan Divine Martial Emperor enjoy the same repose as Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: A senior duke went to the western-step mat, removed his shoes, knelt, laid his sword on the mat, ascended, and knelt north of the throne to congratulate the emperor: "Official So-and-so, your servant So-and-so, says: At the year's first fortune, blessings renew; may Your Majesty the Kaiyuan Divine Martial Emperor share Heaven's repose."

sentences.zh: 」冬至云：「天正長至，伏惟陛下如日之升。

translations.literal: " On the winter solstice he said: "The celestial first day reaches its fullness; may Your Majesty rise like the sun."
translations.idiomatic: " On the winter solstice he said: "The celestial new year has reached its height; may Your Majesty ascend like the sun."

sentences.zh: 」乃降階詣席，跪，佩劍，俯伏，興，納舄，復位。

translations.literal: " He then descended the steps to the mat, knelt, girded his sword, prostrated himself, rose, put on his shoes, and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went down to the mat, knelt, girded his sword, prostrated, rose, put on his shoes, and returned to station.

sentences.zh: 在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: All in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: All present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中前承詔，降，詣群官東北，西面，稱「有制」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant came forward to receive the edict, descended, went to the northeast of the officials, faced west, and said "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant advanced to take the edict, went down to the officials' northeast, faced west, and announced: "By edict."

sentences.zh: 在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: All in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: All present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 宣制曰：「履新之慶，與公等同之。

translations.literal: The edict was proclaimed: "The joy of treading the new—share it with you all alike."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "The joy of the new year—share it equally with you."

sentences.zh: 」冬至云：「履長。

translations.literal: " On the winter solstice it said: "Treading the fullness."
translations.idiomatic: " On the winter solstice it read: "Treading the year's height."

sentences.zh: 」在位者皆再拜，舞蹈，三稱萬歲，又再拜。

translations.literal: " All in attendance bowed twice, performed the dance, thrice shouted "Ten thousand years," and bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: " All present bowed twice, danced, shouted "Long live the emperor" three times, and bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 初，群官將朝，中書侍郎以諸州鎮表別為一桉，俟於右延明門外，給事中以祥瑞桉俟于左延明門外，侍郎、給事中俱就侍臣班。

translations.literal: Earlier, as officials were about to attend court, the Secretariat Vice Director set out a separate table for provincial memorials and waited outside the right Yanming Gate; the Imperial Receptionist set out a table for auspicious omens outside the left Yanming Gate; the Vice Director and Receptionist both joined the attendant ministers' ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Before the audience, the Secretariat Vice Director prepared a separate table for provincial memorials outside the right Yanming Gate; the Imperial Receptionist prepared a table for auspicious reports outside the left Yanming Gate; both joined the attendant ministers' formation.

sentences.zh: 初入，戶部以諸州貢物陳於太極門東東、西廟，禮部以諸蕃貢物可執者，蕃客執入就位，其餘陳於朝堂前。

translations.literal: On first entry the Ministry of Revenue displayed provincial tribute east and west of the Taiji Gate shrines; the Ministry of Rites had foreign tribute that could be carried brought in by foreign guests to their places, the rest displayed before the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: At first entry the Revenue Ministry arrayed provincial tribute east and west of the Taiji Gate shrines; the Rites Ministry had portable foreign tribute carried in by guests to their stations, the rest set before the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 上公將入門，中書侍郎、給事中皆降，各引其桉入，詣東、西階下立。

translations.literal: As the senior duke was about to enter the gate, the Secretariat Vice Director and Imperial Receptionist both descended, each led in his table, and stood below the eastern and western steps.
translations.idiomatic: When the senior duke was about to enter, the Vice Director and Receptionist descended, each led in his table, and stood below the east and west steps.

sentences.zh: 上公將升賀，中書令、黃門侍郎俱降，各立，取所奏之文以次升。

translations.literal: As the senior duke was about to ascend to offer congratulations, the Secretariat Director and Yellow Gate Vice Director both descended, each stood, took the memorial to be presented, and ascended in order.
translations.idiomatic: When the senior duke was about to ascend to congratulate, the Secretariat Director and Yellow Gate Vice Director descended, stood, took up the documents to be presented, and ascended in turn.

sentences.zh: 上公已賀，中書令前跪奏諸方表，黃門侍郎又進跪奏祥瑞，俱降，置所奏之文於桉。

translations.literal: After the senior duke had offered congratulations, the Secretariat Director advanced and knelt to present the regional memorials; the Yellow Gate Vice Director again advanced and knelt to present auspicious omens; both descended and set the presented documents on the tables.
translations.idiomatic: After the senior duke's congratulations, the Secretariat Director knelt forward to present regional memorials; the Yellow Gate Vice Director again knelt to present auspicious reports; both descended and laid the documents on the tables.

sentences.zh: 侍郎與給事中引桉退至東、西階前，桉出。

translations.literal: The Vice Director and Receptionist led the tables back before the eastern and western steps, and the tables were removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director and Receptionist withdrew the tables to the east and west steps, then removed them.

sentences.zh: 初，侍中已宣制，朝集使及蕃客皆再拜。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the Palace Attendant had proclaimed the edict, assembly envoys and foreign guests all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: After the Palace Attendant had proclaimed the edict, assembly envoys and foreign guests bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書進詣階間跪奏，稱：「戶部尚書臣某言：諸州貢物請付所司。

translations.literal: The Minister of Revenue advanced to the foot of the steps, knelt, and memorialized: "The Minister of Revenue, your servant So-and-so, says: The provincial tribute—may it be handed to the relevant offices."
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Minister advanced to the steps, knelt, and said: "Revenue Minister, your servant So-and-so, requests that provincial tribute be delivered to the proper offices."

sentences.zh: 」侍中前承制，退，稱：「制曰可。

translations.literal: " The Palace Attendant came forward to receive the edict, withdrew, and said: "The edict says: Approved."
translations.idiomatic: " The Palace Attendant took the edict, withdrew, and announced: "The edict says: Approved."

sentences.zh: 」禮部尚書以次進詣階間，跪奏，稱「禮部尚書臣某言：諸蕃貢物請付所司。

translations.literal: " The Minister of Rites next advanced to the foot of the steps, knelt, and memorialized: "The Minister of Rites, your servant So-and-so, says: The foreign tribute—may it be handed to the relevant offices."
translations.idiomatic: " The Rites Minister advanced in turn to the steps, knelt, and said: "Rites Minister, your servant So-and-so, requests that foreign tribute be delivered to the proper offices."

sentences.zh: 」侍中前承制，退，稱：「制曰可。

translations.literal: " The Palace Attendant came forward to receive the edict, withdrew, and said: "The edict says: Approved."
translations.idiomatic: " The Palace Attendant took the edict, withdrew, and announced: "The edict says: Approved."

sentences.zh: 」太府帥其屬受諸州及諸蕃貢物出歸仁、納義門，執物者隨之。

translations.literal: The Grand Storehouse led its subordinates to receive the provincial and foreign tribute and exit through the Guiren and Nayi Gates; those carrying items followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Storehouse led its staff to take provincial and foreign tribute out through the Guiren and Nayi Gates, carriers following.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」通事舍人以次引北面位者出。

translations.literal: " Protocol Aides led out those in north-facing positions in order.
translations.idiomatic: " Protocol Aides led out those in north-facing stations in sequence.

sentences.zh: 侍中前，跪奏稱：「侍中臣某言：禮畢。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt, and memorialized: "The Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: The rites are complete."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt, and reported: "Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: The rites are complete."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝降座，禦輿入自東房，侍臣從至閣。

translations.literal: The emperor left the throne; the imperial carriage entered from the eastern chamber; attendant ministers followed to the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the throne; the imperial carriage returned through the east chamber; attendant ministers followed to the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 引東、西面位者以次出，蕃客先出。

translations.literal: Those in east- and west-facing positions were led out in order; foreign guests exited first.
translations.idiomatic: East- and west-facing groups were led out in order; foreign guests left first.

sentences.zh: 冬至，不奏祥瑞，無諸方表。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice, auspicious omens were not presented and there were no regional memorials.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice, auspicious reports were omitted and regional memorials were not presented.

sentences.zh: 其會，則太樂令設登歌於殿上，二舞入，立于縣南。

translations.literal: For the feast, the Director of Imperial Music set ascending song on the hall; the two dance troupes entered and stood south of the bells.
translations.idiomatic: At the feast the Director of Imperial Music set hall music for ascending song; the two dance companies entered and stood south of the bells.

sentences.zh: 尚舍設群官升殿者座：文官三品以上又御座東南，西向；

translations.literal: The Imperial Household Service set seats for officials ascending the hall: civil officials of the third rank and above again southeast of the throne, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household Service placed seats for hall ascent: third-rank civil officials and above southeast of the throne, facing west;

sentences.zh: 介公、酅公在御座西南，東向；

translations.literal: the Duke of Jie and the Duke of Xi southwest of the throne, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi southwest of the throne, facing east;

sentences.zh: 武官三品以上又於其後；

translations.literal: military officials of the third rank and above again behind them;
translations.idiomatic: third-rank military officials and above stood behind them;

sentences.zh: 朝集使、都督、刺史，蕃客三等以上，座如立位。

translations.literal: assembly envoys, governors, prefects, and foreign guests of the third grade and above—seating as for standing positions.
translations.idiomatic: assembly envoys, governors, prefects, and third-grade foreign guests sat as for their standing stations.

sentences.zh: 設不升殿者座各於其位。

translations.literal: Seats were also set at each station for those not ascending the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Seats were set at each station for those not ascending the hall.

sentences.zh: 又設群官解劍席於縣之西北，橫街之南。

translations.literal: Sword-removal mats for officials were again set northwest of the bells, south of the transverse street.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' sword-removal mats were again placed northwest of the bells, south of the transverse street.

sentences.zh: 尚食設壽尊於殿上東序之端，西向；

translations.literal: The Imperial Provisioner set the longevity wine vessel at the east end of the hall sequence, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Provisioner set the longevity wine vessel at the east end of the hall row, facing west;

sentences.zh: 設坫于尊南，加爵一。

translations.literal: a libation stand was set south of the vessel, with one goblet added.
translations.idiomatic: a libation stand south of the vessel, with one goblet placed upon it.

sentences.zh: 太官令設升殿者酒尊於東、西廂，近北；

translations.literal: The Grand Kitchen Steward set wine vessels for those ascending the hall in the east and west wings, near the north;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Kitchen Steward set wine for hall guests in the east and west wings, near the north;

sentences.zh: 設在庭群官酒尊各於其座之南。

translations.literal: wine vessels for officials in the courtyard were set south of each seat.
translations.idiomatic: courtyard officials' wine vessels were set south of each seat.

sentences.zh: 皆有坫、冪，俱障以帷。

translations.literal: All had stands and covers, screened with curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Each had stands and covers, all screened with curtains.

sentences.zh: 吏部兵部戶部主客贊群官、客使俱出次，通事舍人引就朝堂前位，又引非升殿者次入就位。

translations.literal: The Ministries of Personnel, War, Revenue, and Receptions ushered officials and envoys from their ranks; Protocol Aides led them to positions before the audience hall, then led those not ascending the hall to enter and take their places.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel, War, Revenue, and Receptions directors ushered officials and envoys; Protocol Aides led them to the audience-hall stations, then brought in those not ascending the hall.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized on the board: "The outer rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported on the board: "Outer preparations complete."

sentences.zh: 皇帝改服通天冠、絳紗袍，禦輿出自西房，即御座。

translations.literal: The emperor changed into the open-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, rode the imperial carriage out from the western chamber, and took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed to the open-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, came out from the west chamber by carriage, and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 典儀一人升就東階上，通事舍人引公、王以下及諸客使以次入就位。

translations.literal: One Master of Ceremonies ascended the eastern steps; Protocol Aides led dukes, princes, and below and all envoys and guests to enter in order to their places.
translations.idiomatic: One Master of Ceremonies ascended the east steps; Protocol Aides led dukes, princes, and below, with all envoys and guests, in to their stations.

sentences.zh: 侍中進，當御座前北面跪奏，稱：「侍中臣某言：請延諸公、王等升。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt north of the throne, and memorialized: "The Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: Request that the dukes, princes, and others ascend."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt before the throne, and said: "Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, requests that dukes, princes, and the rest ascend."

sentences.zh: 」又侍中稱：「制曰可。

translations.literal: " The Palace Attendant again said: "The edict says: Approved."
translations.idiomatic: " The Palace Attendant announced: "The edict says: Approved."

sentences.zh: 」侍中詣東階上，西面，稱：「制延公、王等升殿上。

translations.literal: " The Palace Attendant went to the top of the eastern steps, faced west, and said: "By edict, dukes, princes, and others ascend to the hall."
translations.idiomatic: " The Palace Attendant went to the east steps, faced west, and proclaimed: "By edict, dukes, princes, and others ascend the hall."

sentences.zh: 」典儀承傳，階下贊者又承傳，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies relayed it; announcers below the steps again relayed it; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies passed the word; stairwell announcers relayed it; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 應升殿者詣東、西階，至解劍席，脫舄，解劍，升。

translations.literal: Those who should ascend the hall went to the eastern and western steps, reached the sword-removal mats, removed shoes and swords, and ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Those entitled to ascend went to the east and west steps, reached the sword-removal mats, removed shoes and swords, and went up.

sentences.zh: 上公一人升階，少東，西面，立於座後。

translations.literal: One senior duke ascended the steps, slightly to the east, faced west, and stood behind the seats.
translations.idiomatic: One senior duke ascended, stood slightly east, faced west, and waited behind the seats.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿進詣階間，跪奏稱：「臣某言：請賜群臣上壽。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Household Bureau advanced to the foot of the steps, knelt, and memorialized: "Your servant So-and-so says: Request permission to offer longevity wine to the ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Household Bureau advanced to the steps, knelt, and said: "Your servant So-and-so requests leave to offer longevity wine to the ministers."

sentences.zh: 」侍中稱：「制曰可。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant said: "The edict says: Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced: "The edict says: Approved."

sentences.zh: 」光祿卿退，升詣酒尊所，西向立。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Household Bureau withdrew, ascended to the wine vessel, and stood facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Director withdrew, ascended to the wine vessel, and stood facing west.

sentences.zh: 上公酒尊所，北面。

translations.literal: At the senior duke's wine vessel, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: At the senior duke's wine station, facing north.

sentences.zh: 尚食酌酒一爵授上公，上公受爵，進前，北面授殿中監，殿中監受爵，進，置御前，上公退，北面跪稱：「某官臣某等稽首言：元正首祚冬至云：「天正長至。

translations.literal: The Imperial Provisioner poured one goblet of wine and handed it to the senior duke; the senior duke received the goblet, advanced, and facing north handed it to the Director of the Palace Domestic Service; the Director received the goblet, advanced, and set it before the throne; the senior duke withdrew, knelt facing north, and said: "Such-and-such an official, your servant So-and-so and others bow and say: On the first fortune of the year—on the winter solstice: "The celestial first day reaches its fullness."
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Provisioner poured one goblet and gave it to the senior duke; he received it, advanced, and facing north passed it to the Director of the Palace Domestic Service; the Director set it before the throne; the senior duke withdrew, knelt north, and said: "Official So-and-so, your servant So-and-so and others bow and say: At the year's first fortune—on the winter solstice: "The celestial new year has reached its height."

sentences.zh: 」，臣某等不勝大慶，謹上千秋萬歲壽。

translations.literal: , your servants So-and-so and others cannot contain our great rejoicing and respectfully offer a thousand autumns and ten thousand years of life."
translations.idiomatic: , we cannot contain our great joy and respectfully offer long life for a thousand autumns and ten thousand years."

sentences.zh: 」再拜，在位者皆再拜，立于席後。

translations.literal: " Bowed twice; all in attendance bowed twice and stood behind their mats.
translations.idiomatic: " They bowed twice; all present bowed twice and stood behind their mats.

sentences.zh: 侍中前承制，退稱：「敬舉公等之觴。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant came forward to receive the edict, withdrew, and said: "Respectfully raise your goblets, lords."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant took the edict, withdrew, and said: "Raise your cups, lords."

sentences.zh: 」在位者又再拜。

translations.literal: All in attendance bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: All present bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 殿中監取爵奉進，皇帝舉酒，在位者皆舞蹈，三稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Domestic Service took the goblet and presented it; the emperor raised the wine; all in attendance performed the dance and thrice shouted "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Domestic Service presented the goblet; the emperor drank; all present danced and shouted "Long live the emperor" three times.

sentences.zh: 皇帝舉酒訖，殿中監進，受虛爵，以授尚食，尚食受爵於坫。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished the wine, the Director of the Palace Domestic Service advanced, received the empty goblet, and handed it to the Imperial Provisioner, who received the goblet at the libation stand.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had drunk, the Director advanced, took the empty goblet, and passed it to the Imperial Provisioner, who set it on the libation stand.

sentences.zh: 初，殿中監受虛爵，殿上典儀唱：「再拜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Director of the Palace Domestic Service received the empty goblet, the Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Director took the empty goblet, the Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」階下贊者承傳，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " Announcers below the steps relayed it; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " Stairwell announcers passed the word; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 上公就座後立，殿上典儀唱：「就座。

translations.literal: After the senior duke had taken his seat and stood behind it, the Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "Take your seats.
translations.idiomatic: After the senior duke stood behind his seat, the Hall Master called: "Take your seats.

sentences.zh: 」階下贊者承傳，俱就座。

translations.literal: " Announcers below the steps relayed it; all took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: " Stairwell announcers relayed it; all sat down.

sentences.zh: 歌者琴瑟升坐，笙管立階間。

translations.literal: Singers with zithers and lutes ascended and sat; pipes and flutes stood between the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Zither and lute players ascended and sat; pipe players stood between the steps.

sentences.zh: 尚食進，酒至階，殿上典儀唱：「酒至，興。

translations.literal: The Imperial Provisioner advanced; when the wine reached the steps, the Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "Wine has arrived—rise.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Provisioner advanced; as wine reached the steps, the Hall Master called: "Wine arrives—rise.

sentences.zh: 」階下贊者承傳，坐者皆俯伏，起，立于席後。

translations.literal: " Announcers below the steps relayed it; seated participants all prostrated themselves, rose, and stood behind their mats.
translations.idiomatic: " Stairwell announcers relayed it; seated guests prostrated, rose, and stood behind their mats.

sentences.zh: 殿中監到階省酒，尚食奉酒進，皇帝舉酒。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Domestic Service went to the steps to inspect the wine; the Imperial Provisioner presented the wine; the emperor raised the wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Domestic Service inspected the wine at the steps; the Imperial Provisioner presented it; the emperor drank.

sentences.zh: 太官令又行群官酒，酒至，殿上典儀唱：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Grand Kitchen Steward again circulated wine among the officials; when the wine arrived, the Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Kitchen Steward circulated wine to the officials; when it arrived, the Hall Master called: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」階下贊者承傳，在位者皆再拜，搢笏受觶。

translations.literal: " Announcers below the steps relayed it; all in attendance bowed twice, inserted their tablets, and received the goblets.
translations.idiomatic: " Stairwell announcers relayed it; all present bowed twice, tucked their tablets, and received goblets.

sentences.zh: 殿上典儀唱：「就座。

translations.literal: The Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "Take your seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall Master called: "Take your seats.

sentences.zh: 」階下贊者承傳，皆就座。

translations.literal: " Announcers below the steps relayed it; all took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: " Stairwell announcers relayed it; all sat down.

sentences.zh: 皇帝舉酒，尚食進，受虛爵，復於坫。

translations.literal: The emperor raised the wine; the Imperial Provisioner advanced, received the empty goblet, and returned it to the libation stand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drank; the Imperial Provisioner took the empty goblet and returned it to the stand.

sentences.zh: 觴行三周，尚食進禦食，食至階，殿上典儀唱：「食至，興。

translations.literal: After three rounds of goblets, the Imperial Provisioner presented imperial food; when food reached the steps, the Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "Food has arrived—rise.
translations.idiomatic: After three rounds of wine, the Imperial Provisioner brought imperial food; as it reached the steps, the Hall Master called: "Food arrives—rise.

sentences.zh: 」階下贊者承傳，坐者皆起，立座後。

translations.literal: " Announcers below the steps relayed it; seated participants all rose and stood behind their seats.
translations.idiomatic: " Stairwell announcers relayed it; seated guests rose and stood behind their seats.

sentences.zh: 殿中監到階省桉，尚食品嘗食訖，以次進置御前。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Domestic Service went to the steps to inspect the tables; the Imperial Provisioner tasted the food, then presented it in order before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Director inspected the tables at the steps; the Imperial Provisioner tasted the food, then presented it in sequence before the throne.

sentences.zh: 太官令又行群安桉，設食訖，殿上典儀唱：「就座。

translations.literal: The Grand Kitchen Steward again circulated the officials' tables; when food was set, the Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "Take your seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Kitchen Steward again served the officials' tables; when food was ready, the Hall Master called: "Take your seats.

sentences.zh: 」階下贊者承傳，皆就座。

translations.literal: " Announcers below the steps relayed it; all took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: " Stairwell announcers relayed it; all sat down.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乃飯，上下俱飯。

translations.literal: The emperor then ate; above and below all ate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ate; all above and below ate.

sentences.zh: 禦食畢，仍行酒，遂設庶羞，二舞作。

translations.literal: When imperial food was finished, wine was again circulated; then assorted dishes were set and the two dances performed.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial meal, wine continued; assorted dishes were served and the two dance troupes performed.

sentences.zh: 若賜酒，侍中承詔詣東階上，西面稱：「賜酒。

translations.literal: If wine was bestowed, the Palace Attendant received the edict, went to the top of the eastern steps, faced west, and said: "Wine is granted.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was granted, the Palace Attendant took the edict to the east steps, faced west, and announced: "Wine is granted.

sentences.zh: 」殿上典儀承傳，階下贊者又承傳，坐者皆起，再拜，立，受觶，就席坐飲，立，授虛爵，又再拜，就座。

translations.literal: " The Hall Master of Ceremonies relayed it; announcers below the steps again relayed it; seated participants all rose, bowed twice, stood, received goblets, sat at their mats and drank, stood, handed over empty goblets, bowed twice again, and took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: " The Hall Master passed the word; stairwell announcers relayed it; seated guests rose, bowed twice, stood, received goblets, sat to drink, stood, returned empty goblets, bowed twice again, and sat.

sentences.zh: 酒行十二遍。

translations.literal: Wine was circulated twelve times.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve rounds of wine were served.

sentences.zh: 會畢，殿上典儀唱：「可起。

translations.literal: When the feast was complete, the Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "You may rise.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended, the Hall Master called: "You may rise.

sentences.zh: 」階下贊者承傳，上下皆起，降階，佩劍，納舄，復位。

translations.literal: " Announcers below the steps relayed it; all above and below rose, descended the steps, girded swords, put on shoes, and returned to their places.
translations.idiomatic: " Stairwell announcers relayed it; all rose, descended, girded swords, put on shoes, and returned to station.

sentences.zh: 位於殿庭者，仍立于席後。

translations.literal: Those positioned in the hall court still stood behind their mats.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the courtyard still stood behind their mats.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」贊者承傳，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " Announcers relayed it; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " Announcers passed the word; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 若有賜物，侍中前承制，降，詣群官東北，西面，稱：「有制。

translations.literal: If gifts were bestowed, the Palace Attendant came forward to receive the edict, descended, went to the northeast of the officials, faced west, and said: "There is an edict.
translations.idiomatic: When gifts were granted, the Palace Attendant took the edict, went to the officials' northeast, faced west, and announced: "By edict.

sentences.zh: 」在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " All in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中宣制，又再拜，以次出。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant proclaimed the edict; they bowed twice again and exited in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant read the edict; all bowed twice again and left in order.

sentences.zh: 侍中前，跪奏稱：「侍中臣某言：禮畢。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt, and memorialized: "The Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: The rites are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt, and reported: "Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: The rites are complete.

sentences.zh: 」皇帝興，禦輿入自東房，東、西面位者以次出。

translations.literal: " The emperor rose; the imperial carriage entered from the eastern chamber; those in east- and west-facing positions exited in order.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor rose; the imperial carriage returned through the east chamber; east- and west-facing groups left in sequence.

sentences.zh: 皇帝若服翼善冠、袴褶，則京官袴褶，朝集使公服。

translations.literal: If the emperor wore the Goodness-Wing cap and trousers-robe, capital officials wore trousers-robes and assembly envoys wore court dress.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor wore the Goodness-Wing cap and military dress, capital officials wore military dress and assembly envoys wore court robes.

sentences.zh: 設九部樂，則去樂縣，無警蹕。

translations.literal: If the nine-section music was set up, the bell frame was removed and there was no road clearance.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine-section ensemble was used, the courtyard bells were removed and road clearance was omitted.

sentences.zh: 太樂令帥九部伎立于左、右延明門外，群官初唱萬歲，太樂令即引九部伎聲作而入，各就座，以次作。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Music led the nine-section performers to stand outside the left and right Yanming Gates; when officials first shouted "Ten thousand years," the Director immediately led the nine-section performers in with sound, each took his seat, and performed in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Music arrayed the nine-section troupe outside the left and right Yanming Gates; at the first shout of "Long live the emperor," he led the troupe in playing; each took station and performed in turn.

sentences.zh: 臨軒冊皇太子

translations.literal: Enthronement at the Hall to Invest the Crown Prince
translations.idiomatic: Investiture of the Crown Prince at the Imperial Hall

sentences.zh: 臨軒冊皇太子。

translations.literal: Enthronement at the hall to invest the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is invested at the imperial hall.

sentences.zh: 有司卜日，告於天地宗廟。

translations.literal: The relevant offices divined the day and announced it to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Offices divined the date and announced it to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 前一日，尚舍設禦幄於大極殿，有司設太子次於東朝堂之北，西向。

translations.literal: On the previous day the Imperial Household Service set the imperial canopy in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the relevant offices set the crown prince's waiting station north of the eastern audience hall, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the Imperial Household Service erected the imperial enclosure in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; officials placed the crown prince's waiting station north of the eastern audience hall, facing west.

sentences.zh: 又設版位於大橫街之南，展縣，設桉，陳車輿，及文武群官、朝集、蕃客之次位，皆如加元服之日。

translations.literal: A presentation tablet was also set south of the great transverse street; bells were suspended, tables set, carriages arrayed, and ranks for civil and military officials, assembly envoys, and foreign guests—as on the day of coming-of-age.
translations.idiomatic: A presentation station was set south of the great transverse street; bells hung, tables set, carriages lined up, and ranks for officials, assembly envoys, and foreign guests—as for the coming-of-age ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其日，前二刻，宮官服其器服，諸衛率各勒所部陳於庭。

translations.literal: On that day, two quarters before the hour, palace officers donned their regalia; commanders of the guard units each arrayed their detachments in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Two quarters before the hour, palace officers donned regalia; guard commanders arrayed their units in the court.

sentences.zh: 左庶子奏「請中嚴」。

translations.literal: The Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent memorialized: "Request inner vigilance."
translations.idiomatic: The Left Guardian memorialized: "Request inner vigilance."

sentences.zh: 侍衛之官奉迎，僕進金路，內率一人執刀。

translations.literal: Guards came to welcome; attendants brought the golden carriage; one inner-rate officer held the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Guard officers came to receive him; attendants brought the golden carriage; one inner-rate officer bore the blade.

sentences.zh: 贊善奏「發引」。

translations.literal: The Good Companion memorialized: "Set out the procession."
translations.idiomatic: The Good Companion reported: "Begin the procession."

sentences.zh: 令侍臣上馬，庶子承令。

translations.literal: Attendant ministers were ordered to mount; the Guardian received the command.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant ministers were ordered to mount; the Guardian conveyed the command.

sentences.zh: 其餘略如皇帝出宮之禮。

translations.literal: The rest followed the emperor's departure from the palace in general.
translations.idiomatic: The rest followed the emperor's palace departure rites in general.

sentences.zh: 皇太子遠遊冠、絳紗袍，三師導，三少從，鳴鐃而行。

translations.literal: The crown prince wore the distant-travel cap and crimson gauze robe; the three tutors led, the three juniors followed, and bells sounded as they proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wore the distant-travel cap and crimson gauze robe; three tutors led and three juniors followed, bells sounding as they went.

sentences.zh: 降路入次，亦如鑾駕。

translations.literal: He descended from the carriage and entered the waiting station, as for the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: He descended and entered the waiting station, as for the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 其日，列黃麾大仗，侍中請「中嚴」。

translations.literal: On that day yellow-banner great halberds were arrayed; the Palace Attendant requested "inner vigilance."
translations.idiomatic: That day yellow-banner great halberds were posted; the Palace Attendant requested inner vigilance.

sentences.zh: 有司與群官皆入就位。

translations.literal: The relevant offices and all officials entered and took their places.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and all ministers entered and took station.

sentences.zh: 三師、三少導從，皇太子立于殿門外之東，西向。

translations.literal: The three tutors and three juniors led and followed; the crown prince stood east of the hall gate, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Three tutors and three juniors escorted him; the crown prince stood east of the hall gate, facing west.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎以冊、寶綬桉立於殿內道北，西面，中書侍郎立桉後。

translations.literal: The Yellow Gate Vice Director stood with the investiture tablet and seal-cord table north of the inner hall passage, facing west; the Secretariat Vice Director stood behind the table.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Gate Vice Director held the investiture tablet and seal-cord table north of the inner passage, facing west; the Secretariat Vice Director stood behind it.

sentences.zh: 侍中乃奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant then memorialized: "The outer rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported: "Outer preparations complete."

sentences.zh: 皇帝服袞冕，出自西房，即御座。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the coronation robe and cap, came out from the western chamber, and took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore full ceremonial dress, came out from the west chamber, and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 皇太子入就位。

translations.literal: The crown prince entered and took his place.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince entered to his station.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」皇太子再拜。

translations.literal: " The crown prince bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: He again said: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: He called again: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " All in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 中書令降，立于皇太子東北，西向。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Director descended and stood northeast of the crown prince, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Director came down and stood northeast of the crown prince, facing west.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎一人引冊、一人引寶綬桉立於其東，西面，以冊授之。

translations.literal: One Secretariat Vice Director led the investiture tablet, one led the seal-cord table and stood east of him, facing west, and handed over the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: One Vice Director led the investiture tablet, one the seal-cord table, standing east of him facing west, and passed the tablet.

sentences.zh: 中書令曰：「有制。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Director said: "There is an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Director announced: "By edict.

sentences.zh: 」皇太子再拜，中書令跪讀冊，皇太子再拜受冊，左庶子受之。

translations.literal: " The crown prince bowed twice; the Secretariat Director knelt and read the tablet; the crown prince bowed twice and received the tablet; the Left Guardian received it.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince bowed twice; the Director knelt and read the tablet; the crown prince bowed twice, received it, and the Left Guardian took it.

sentences.zh: 侍郎以璽綬授中書令，皇太子進受，以授左庶子。

translations.literal: The Vice Director handed the seal cord to the Secretariat Director; the crown prince advanced to receive it and handed it to the Left Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director passed the seal cord to the Director; the crown prince advanced, received it, and gave it to the Left Guardian.

sentences.zh: 皇太子再拜，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The crown prince bowed twice; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bowed twice; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏「禮畢」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized: "The rites are complete."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported: "The rites are complete."

sentences.zh: 皇帝入自東房，在位者以次出。

translations.literal: The emperor entered from the eastern chamber; those in attendance exited in order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned through the east chamber; those present left in order.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御明堂讀時令

translations.literal: The Emperor at the Bright Hall Reads the Seasonal Ordinances
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Reads the Seasonal Ordinances at the Bright Hall

sentences.zh: 皇帝禦明堂讀時令。

translations.literal: The emperor at the Bright Hall reads the seasonal ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reads the seasonal ordinances at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 孟春，禮部尚書先讀令三日奏讀月令，承以宣告。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring the Minister of Rites first read the ordinances for three days and memorialized the reading of the monthly ordinances, which were proclaimed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In early spring the Rites Minister read the ordinances for three days, then memorialized the monthly ordinances for public proclamation.

sentences.zh: 前三日，尚舍設大次於東門外道北，南向；

translations.literal: Three days before, the Imperial Household Service set the great waiting station north of the road outside the eastern gate, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Three days before, the Imperial Household Service set the great waiting pavilion north of the road outside the east gate, facing south;

sentences.zh: 守宮設文、武侍臣次於其後之左、右；

translations.literal: the Palace Maintenance Office set waiting stations for civil and military attendant ministers to its rear, left and right;
translations.idiomatic: the Palace Maintenance Office placed waiting stations for civil and military attendant ministers behind it, left and right;

sentences.zh: 設群官次於璧水東之門外，文官在北，武官在南，俱西上。

translations.literal: ranks for officials were set outside the eastern gate of the Circular Water, civil officials to the north, military officials to the south, all facing west and ascending to the north.
translations.idiomatic: official ranks were set outside the Circular Water's east gate, civil officials north, military south, all facing west with precedence to the north.

sentences.zh: 前一日，設御座于青陽左個，東向。

translations.literal: On the previous day the imperial throne was set in the eastern bay of the Azure Yang Hall, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the throne was set in the eastern bay of the Azure Yang Hall, facing east.

sentences.zh: 三品以上及諸司長官座于堂上：文官座于御座東北，南向；

translations.literal: Officials of the third rank and above and heads of departments were seated in the hall: civil officials northeast of the throne, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank officials and department heads sat in the hall: civil officials northeast of the throne, facing south;

sentences.zh: 武官座于御座之東，北向。

translations.literal: military officials east of the throne, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: military officials east of the throne, facing north.

sentences.zh: 俱重行西上。

translations.literal: All in double rows with precedence to the west and north.
translations.idiomatic: All in double rows, precedence west and north.

sentences.zh: 設刑部郎中讀令座于御座東南，北向，有桉。

translations.literal: A seat for the Ministry of Justice Director of Reading Ordinances was set southeast of the throne, facing north, with a table.
translations.idiomatic: The Justice Ministry ordinance reader's seat was placed southeast of the throne, facing north, with a table.

sentences.zh: 設文官解劍席於醜陛之左，武官于卯陛之右，皆內向。

translations.literal: Sword-removal mats for civil officials were set left of the Chou steps; for military officials right of the Mao steps—both facing inward.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials' sword-removal mats were left of the Chou steps; military officials' right of the Mao steps—both facing inward.

sentences.zh: 太樂令展宮縣于青陽左個之庭，設舉麾位於堂上寅階之西，北向；

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Music suspended palace bells in the court of the Azure Yang eastern bay; a banner-raising station was set west of the hall's Yin steps, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Music hung palace bells in the Azure Yang eastern court; a banner station was set west of the hall's Yin steps, facing north;

sentences.zh: 其一位於樂縣東北，南向。

translations.literal: the chief musician stood northeast of the bell frame, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: the chief musician stood northeast of the bells, facing south.

sentences.zh: 典儀設三品以上及應升坐者位於縣東，文左武右，俱重行西向。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies set positions for third rank and above and those who should ascend to sit east of the bells—civil left, military right—all in double rows facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies placed third rank and above and those ascending to sit east of the bells—civil left, military right—in double rows facing west.

sentences.zh: 非升坐者文官四品、五品位於縣北，六品以下於其東，絕位，俱南向；

translations.literal: Those not ascending: civil officials of the fourth and fifth ranks north of the bells, sixth rank and below east of them, separate rows, all facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Non-ascenders: fourth- and fifth-rank civil officials north of the bells, sixth rank and below east of them in separate rows, all facing south;

sentences.zh: 武官四品、五品于縣南，六品以下於其東，俱北向。

translations.literal: military officials of the fourth and fifth ranks south of the bells, sixth rank and below east of them, all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: fourth- and fifth-rank military officials south of the bells, sixth rank and below east of them, all facing north.

sentences.zh: 皆重行西上。

translations.literal: All in double rows with precedence to the west and north.
translations.idiomatic: All in double rows, precedence west and north.

sentences.zh: 設典儀位於縣之西北，贊者二人在東，差退，俱南向。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies' station was northwest of the bells; two announcers stood to the east, slightly withdrawn, all facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Master's station was northwest of the bells; two announcers east, slightly back, all facing south.

sentences.zh: 奉禮設門外位各於次前，俱每等異位，重行相向，西上。

translations.literal: The Director of Ritual Observances set outside positions before each waiting station, each grade in separate rows facing one another, precedence to the west and north.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Ritual Observances set outside stations before each waiting area, each grade in separate facing rows, precedence west and north.

sentences.zh: 其日，陳小駕，皇帝服青紗袍，佩蒼玉，乘金路出宮，至於大次。

translations.literal: On that day the light imperial carriage was arrayed; the emperor wore the azure gauze robe, wore the azure jade, rode the golden carriage out of the palace, and reached the great waiting station.
translations.idiomatic: That day the light imperial carriage was prepared; the emperor wore azure gauze robe and azure jade, rode the golden carriage from the palace to the great waiting pavilion.

sentences.zh: 文、武五品以上從駕之官皆就門外位，太樂令、工人、協律郎、典儀帥贊者皆先入，群官非升坐者次入，就位。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above who followed the carriage took outside positions; the Director of Imperial Music, musicians, pitch-master, Master of Ceremonies, and announcers all entered first; officials not ascending entered next and took their places.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-rank civil and military officials following the carriage took outside stations; the Music Director, musicians, pitch-master, Master of Ceremonies, and announcers entered first; non-ascending officials followed to station.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中以月令置於桉，覆以帕，立于武官五品東南，郎中立于桉後，北面。

translations.literal: The Justice Ministry Director placed the monthly ordinances on the table, covered with a cloth, and stood southeast of fifth-rank military officials; the director stood behind the table, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Justice ordinance reader placed the monthly ordinances on the table under cloth and stood southeast of fifth-rank military officials; the reader stood behind the table, facing north.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized on the board: "The outer rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported on the board: "Outer preparations complete."

sentences.zh: 皇帝輿入自青龍門，升自寅階，即座。

translations.literal: The emperor's carriage entered through the Azure Dragon Gate; he ascended by the Yin steps and took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage entered through the Azure Dragon Gate; the emperor ascended the Yin steps and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎置寶於前。

translations.literal: The Talisman-and-Seal Officer set the seals before him.
translations.idiomatic: The Talisman-and-Seal Officer set the seals before him.

sentences.zh: 典儀升，立于左個東北，南向。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies ascended and stood northeast of the eastern bay, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies went up and stood northeast of the eastern bay, facing south.

sentences.zh: 公、王以下入就西面位。

translations.literal: Dukes, princes, and below entered to the west-facing positions.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, princes, and below entered to west-facing stations.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」贊者承傳，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " Announcers relayed it; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " Announcers passed the word; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中前，跪奏稱：「侍中臣某言：請延公、王等升。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt, and memorialized: "The Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: Request that the dukes, princes, and others ascend.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt, and said: "Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, requests that dukes, princes, and the rest ascend.

sentences.zh: 」又侍中稱：「制曰可。

translations.literal: " The Palace Attendant again said: "The edict says: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The Palace Attendant announced: "The edict says: Approved.

sentences.zh: 」侍中詣左個東北，南向稱：「詔延公、王等升。

translations.literal: " The Palace Attendant went to the northeast of the eastern bay, faced south, and said: "By edict, dukes, princes, and others ascend.
translations.idiomatic: " The Palace Attendant went to the northeast of the eastern bay, faced south, and proclaimed: "By edict, dukes, princes, and others ascend.

sentences.zh: 」典儀傳，贊者承傳，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " The Master of Ceremonies relayed it; announcers relayed it; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The Master passed the word; announcers relayed it; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 西面位者各詣其階，解劍，脫舄，升，立於座後。

translations.literal: Those in west-facing positions each went to their steps, removed swords and shoes, ascended, and stood behind their seats.
translations.idiomatic: West-facing groups went to their steps, removed swords and shoes, ascended, and stood behind their seats.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中引桉進，立於卯階下。

translations.literal: The Justice Ministry Director led the table forward and stood below the Mao steps.
translations.idiomatic: The ordinance reader led the table forward and stood below the Mao steps.

sentences.zh: 侍中跪奏「請讀月令」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant knelt and memorialized: "Request to read the monthly ordinances."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant knelt and memorialized: "Request to read the monthly ordinances."

sentences.zh: 又侍中稱：「制曰可。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant again said: "The edict says: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced: "The edict says: Approved.

sentences.zh: 」刑部郎中再拜，解劍，俯，脫舄，取令，升自卯階，詣席南，北向跪，置令於桉，立于席後。

translations.literal: " The Justice Ministry Director bowed twice, removed his sword, bowed low, removed his shoes, took the ordinances, ascended by the Mao steps, went south of the mat, knelt facing north, set the ordinances on the table, and stood behind the mat.
translations.idiomatic: " The reader bowed twice, removed his sword, bowed, removed his shoes, took the ordinances, ascended the Mao steps, knelt north at the mat, set them on the table, and stood behind it.

sentences.zh: 堂上典儀唱：「就座。

translations.literal: The Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "Take your seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall Master called: "Take your seats.

sentences.zh: 」公、王以下及刑部郎中並就座。

translations.literal: " Dukes, princes, and below and the Justice Ministry Director all took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: " Dukes, princes, and below, with the reader, all sat down.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中讀令，每句一絕，使言聲可了。

translations.literal: The Justice Ministry Director read the ordinances, pausing at each phrase so the voice could be understood.
translations.idiomatic: The reader recited the ordinances, pausing at each phrase so every word was clear.

sentences.zh: 讀訖，堂上典儀唱：「可起。

translations.literal: When reading was finished, the Hall Master of Ceremonies called: "You may rise.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading ended, the Hall Master called: "You may rise.

sentences.zh: 」王、公以下皆起。

translations.literal: " Princes, dukes, and below all rose.
translations.idiomatic: " Princes, dukes, and below all rose.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中以令置於桉，與群官佩劍，納舄，復於位。

translations.literal: The Justice Ministry Director set the ordinances on the table; with the officials he girded swords, put on shoes, and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The reader set the ordinances on the table; officials girded swords, put on shoes, and returned to station.

sentences.zh: 典儀曰；

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said;
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies called;

sentences.zh: 「再拜。

translations.literal: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: " All in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 西面位者出。

translations.literal: Those in west-facing positions exited.
translations.idiomatic: West-facing groups departed.

sentences.zh: 侍中跪奏稱：「侍中臣某言：禮畢。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant knelt and memorialized: "The Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: The rites are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant knelt and reported: "Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: The rites are complete.

sentences.zh: 」皇帝降座，禦輿出之便次，南、北面位者以次出。

translations.literal: " The emperor left the throne; the imperial carriage went to the convenience station; those in south- and north-facing positions exited in order.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor left the throne; the carriage went to the rest station; south- and north-facing groups left in order.

sentences.zh: 自仲春以後，每月各居其位，皆冠通天，服、玉之色如其時。

translations.literal: From the second month of spring onward, each month occupied its proper position; all wore the open-heaven cap; robe and jade colors matched the season.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-spring each month used its proper hall; all wore the open-heaven cap; robes and jade matched the season.

sentences.zh: 若四時之孟月及季夏土王讀五時令於明堂，亦如之。

translations.literal: If in the first month of each season and in the last month of summer when Earth is king the five seasonal ordinances were read at the Bright Hall, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the five seasonal ordinances at the Bright Hall in each season's first month and in late summer when Earth reigned followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 皇帝親養三老五更於太學

translations.literal: The Emperor Personally Nourishes the Three Elders and Five Seniors at the Imperial Academy
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Personally Feeds the Three Elders and Five Seniors at the Imperial Academy

sentences.zh: 皇帝親養三老五更於太學。

translations.literal: The emperor personally nourishes the three elders and five seniors at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally feeds the three elders and five seniors at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 所司先奏三師、三公致仕者，用其德行及年高者一人為三老，次一人為五更，五品以上致仕者為國老，六品以下致仕者為庶老。

translations.literal: The relevant offices first memorialized retired grand tutors and grand preceptors; of those whose virtue and age were highest, one was made Three Elder and the next Five Senior; retired officials of the fifth rank and above were State Elders, sixth rank and below were Common Elders.
translations.idiomatic: Offices first nominated retired grand tutors and preceptors; the most virtuous and eldest became Three Elder and Five Senior; fifth-rank retirees were State Elders, sixth rank and below Common Elders.

sentences.zh: 尚食具牢饌。

translations.literal: The Imperial Provisioner prepared the great feast.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Provisioner prepared the great feast.

sentences.zh: 前三日，尚舍設大次於學堂之後，隨地之宜。

translations.literal: Three days before, the Imperial Household Service set the great waiting station behind the academy hall, as the site allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before, the Imperial Household Service set the great waiting pavilion behind the academy, as space allowed.

sentences.zh: 設三老、五更次於南門外之西，群老又於其後，皆東向。

translations.literal: Waiting stations for the Three Elder and Five Senior were set west of the southern gate outside; group elders again behind them—all facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Stations for the Three Elder and Five Senior were west of the south gate outside; other elders behind them—all facing east.

sentences.zh: 文官于門外之東，武官在群老之西，重行，東西向，皆北上。

translations.literal: Civil officials east of the gate outside; military officials west of the group elders, in double rows east and west facing, all ascending to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials east of the outer gate; military west of the elder group in double rows, all facing with precedence north.

sentences.zh: 前一日，設御座於堂上東序，西向，莞筵藻席。

translations.literal: On the previous day the imperial throne was set on the hall's eastern sequence, facing west, with rush mats and water-plant edging.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the throne was set on the hall's east row, facing west, with rush mats and embroidered edging.

sentences.zh: 三老座於西楹之東，近北，南向；

translations.literal: The Three Elder sat east of the western pillar, near the north, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elder sat east of the west pillar, near the north, facing south;

sentences.zh: 五更座於西階上，東向；

translations.literal: the Five Senior sat on the western steps, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: the Five Senior sat on the west steps, facing east;

sentences.zh: 國老三人座於三老西階，不屬焉。

translations.literal: three State Elders sat on the Three Elder's western steps, not connected.
translations.idiomatic: three State Elders sat on steps west of the Three Elder, not adjoining.

sentences.zh: 皆莞筵藻席。

translations.literal: All had rush mats and water-plant edging.
translations.idiomatic: All had rush mats with embroidered edging.

sentences.zh: 眾國老座於堂下西階之西，東面北上，皆蒲筵緇布純，加莞席。

translations.literal: The mass of State Elders sat west of the western steps below the hall, facing east and ascending north, all with rush mats, black borders, and added rush seats.
translations.idiomatic: Other State Elders sat west of the hall steps below, facing east with precedence north, on rush mats with black borders atop rush seats.

sentences.zh: 太樂令展宮縣於庭，設登歌於堂上，如元會。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Music suspended palace bells in the court and set ascending song in the hall, as at the New Year assembly.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Director hung palace bells in the court and set hall ascending song, as at the New Year assembly.

sentences.zh: 典儀設文、武官五品以上位於縣東、西，六品以下在其南，皆重行，西向北上，蕃客位於其南；

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies set positions for civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above east and west of the bells, sixth rank and below south of them, all in double rows facing west and ascending north; foreign guests south of them;
translations.idiomatic: The Master placed fifth-rank civil and military officials east and west of the bells, sixth rank and below south in double rows facing west; foreign guests south of them;

sentences.zh: 諸州使人位於九品之後；

translations.literal: provincial envoys behind the ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: provincial envoys behind ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 學生分位於文、武官之後。

translations.literal: students in ranks behind the civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: students behind the civil and military lines.

sentences.zh: 設門外位如設次。

translations.literal: Outside positions were set as for the waiting stations.
translations.idiomatic: Outside stations matched the waiting layout.

sentences.zh: 又設尊於東楹之西，北向，左玄酒，右坫以置爵。

translations.literal: A wine vessel was also set west of the eastern pillar, facing north; dark liquor on the left, a stand on the right to hold goblets.
translations.idiomatic: A wine vessel was set west of the east pillar, facing north; dark liquor left, a stand right for goblets.

sentences.zh: 其日，鑾駕將至，先置之官就門外位，學生俱青衿服，入就位。

translations.literal: On that day, as the imperial procession was about to arrive, officials already in place took outside positions; students all wore blue-collared robes and entered to their places.
translations.idiomatic: As the procession approached, advance officials took outside stations; students in blue collars entered to place.

sentences.zh: 鑾駕至太學門，回輅南向，侍中跪奏「請降輅」。

translations.literal: When the procession reached the Imperial Academy gate, the carriage turned south; the Palace Attendant knelt and memorialized: "Request to descend from the carriage."
translations.idiomatic: At the academy gate the carriage turned south; the Palace Attendant knelt: "Request to descend."

sentences.zh: 降，入大次。

translations.literal: He descended and entered the great waiting station.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended and entered the great waiting pavilion.

sentences.zh: 文、武五品以上從駕之官皆就門外位，太樂令、工人、二舞入，群官、客使以次入。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above who followed the carriage took outside positions; the Director of Imperial Music, musicians, and two dances entered; officials and envoys entered in order.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-rank followers took outside stations; the Music Director, musicians, and dance troupes entered; officials and envoys followed in order.

sentences.zh: 初，鑾駕出宮，量時刻，遣使迎三老、五更於其第，三老、五更俱服進賢冠，乘安車，前後導從。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the procession left the palace, at the proper time envoys were sent to welcome the Three Elder and Five Senior at their residences; both wore the advancement-worthy cap, rode comfort carriages, and were escorted before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: When the procession left the palace, envoys were sent at the proper hour to fetch the Three Elder and Five Senior; both wore advancement-worthy caps, rode comfort carriages, and were escorted.

sentences.zh: 其國老、庶老則有司預戒之。

translations.literal: State Elders and Common Elders were given prior notice by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: State and Common Elders were notified in advance by the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 鑾駕既至太學，三老、五更及群老等俱赴集，群老各服其服。

translations.literal: When the procession reached the Imperial Academy, the Three Elder, Five Senior, and group elders all assembled; group elders each wore their proper dress.
translations.idiomatic: At the academy the Three Elder, Five Senior, and other elders assembled in proper dress.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿贊三老、五更俱出次，引立于學堂南門外之西，東面北上；

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Office ushered the Three Elder and Five Senior from their waiting stations and led them to stand west of the academy south gate outside, facing east and ascending north;
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrifices Vice Director brought the Three Elder and Five Senior from waiting stations to stand west of the south gate, facing east with precedence north;

sentences.zh: 奉禮贊群老出次，立於三老、五更之後；

translations.literal: the Director of Ritual Observances ushered group elders from waiting stations to stand behind the Three Elder and Five Senior;
translations.idiomatic: the Ritual Director brought other elders out to stand behind them;

sentences.zh: 太常博士引太常卿升，立于學堂北戶之內，當戶北面。

translations.literal: the Sacrifices Doctor led the Sacrifices Director to ascend and stand inside the academy's north door, facing north at the door.
translations.idiomatic: the Sacrifices Doctor led the Director inside the north door to stand facing north at the threshold.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized on the board: "The outer rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported: "Outer preparations complete."

sentences.zh: 皇帝出戶，殿中監進大珪，皇帝執大珪，降，迎三老於門內之東，西面立。

translations.literal: The emperor came out; the Director of the Palace Domestic Service advanced the great scepter; the emperor held the great scepter, descended, and welcomed the Three Elder east inside the gate, standing facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came out; the Palace Domestic Director presented the great scepter; the emperor took it, descended, and welcomed the Three Elder east inside the gate, facing west.

sentences.zh: 侍臣從立于皇帝之後，太常卿與博士退立于左。

translations.literal: Attendant ministers followed and stood behind the emperor; the Sacrifices Director and Doctor withdrew to stand on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant ministers stood behind the emperor; the Sacrifices Director and Doctor withdrew to the left.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更皆杖，各二人夾扶左右，太常少卿引導，敦史執筆以從。

translations.literal: The Three Elder and Five Senior all carried staffs; two men on each side supported them; the Sacrifices Vice Director guided them; the Recorder of Instruction followed with brush in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Three Elder and Five Senior bore staffs, two attendants each side; the Vice Director guided; the Instruction Recorder followed with brush.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更於門西，東面北上，奉禮引群老隨入，立於其後。

translations.literal: The Three Elder and Five Senior west of the gate, facing east and ascending north; the Ritual Director led group elders in after them to stand behind.
translations.idiomatic: They stood west of the gate, facing east; the Ritual Director led other elders in behind.

sentences.zh: 太常卿前奏「請再拜」。

translations.literal: The Sacrifices Director advanced and memorialized: "Request to bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrifices Director advanced: "Request to bow twice."

sentences.zh: 皇帝再拜，三老、五更去杖，攝齊答拜。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed twice; the Three Elder and Five Senior put down staffs, gathered their robes, and returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice; the Three Elder and Five Senior set down staffs, straightened robes, and returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 皇帝揖進，三老在前，五更從，仍杖，夾扶至階，皇帝揖升，俱就座後立。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed and advanced; the Three Elder went before, the Five Senior followed, again with staffs and support to the steps; the emperor bowed and ascended; all stood behind their seats.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed and advanced; the Three Elder led, the Five Senior followed, staffs restored and supported to the steps; the emperor bowed and ascended; all stood behind their seats.

sentences.zh: 皇帝西面再拜三老，三老南面答拜，皇帝又西向肅拜五更，五更答肅拜，俱坐。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed twice westward to the Three Elder; the Three Elder returned the bow facing south; the emperor again performed a respectful bow westward to the Five Senior; the Five Senior returned the respectful bow; all sat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice west to the Three Elder, who returned the bow facing south; he then made a respectful bow west to the Five Senior, who returned it; all sat.

sentences.zh: 三公授幾，九卿正履。

translations.literal: The three grand preceptors presented armrests; the nine ministers straightened footgear.
translations.idiomatic: The three grand preceptors presented armrests; the nine ministers adjusted footgear.

sentences.zh: 殿中監、尚食奉禦進珍羞及黍、稷等，皇帝省之，遂設於三老前。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Imperial Provisioner presented delicacies and millet and glutinous grain; the emperor inspected them, then they were set before the Three Elder.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Domestic Director and Imperial Provisioner presented delicacies with millet and glutinous grain; the emperor inspected them, then they were set before the Three Elder.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣三老座前，執醬而饋，乃詣酒尊所取爵，侍中贊酌酒，皇帝進，執爵而酳。

translations.literal: The emperor went before the Three Elder's seat, held sauce and fed him, then went to the wine vessel, took a goblet; the Palace Attendant announced the pouring; the emperor advanced, held the goblet, and performed the mouth-washing toast.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the Three Elder's seat, offered sauce and fed him, then took a goblet at the wine station; the Palace Attendant announced the pour; the emperor advanced and performed the mouth-washing toast.

sentences.zh: 尚食奉禦以次進珍羞酒食於五更前，國老、庶老等皆坐，又設酒食於前，皆食。

translations.literal: The Imperial Provisioner next presented delicacies and food and wine before the Five Senior; State Elders and Common Elders all sat; food and wine were again set before them; all ate.
translations.idiomatic: The Provisioner next served delicacies, food, and wine before the Five Senior; State and Common Elders sat and were served; all ate.

sentences.zh: 皇帝即座。

translations.literal: The emperor took his seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his seat.

sentences.zh: 三老乃論五孝六順、典訓大綱，格言宣于上，惠音被於下。

translations.literal: The Three Elder then discoursed on the five filial acts and six harmonies and the great outlines of canonical instruction—maxims proclaimed above, gracious sounds reaching below.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elder then expounded the five filial acts, six harmonies, and canonical outlines—maxims voiced above, gracious teaching spread below.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乃虛躬請受，敦史執筆錄善言善行。

translations.literal: The emperor humbly bowed to receive instruction; the Recorder of Instruction wrote down good words and good conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed humbly to receive instruction; the Instruction Recorder wrote down worthy words and deeds.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，三老以下降筵，太常卿引皇帝從以降階，逡巡立於階前。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the Three Elder and below left the mats; the Sacrifices Director led the emperor down the steps and he stood hesitating before the steps.
translations.idiomatic: When rites ended, the Three Elder and below left the mats; the Sacrifices Director led the emperor down to hesitate before the steps.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更出，皇帝升，立於階上，三老、五更出門。

translations.literal: The Three Elder and Five Senior exited; the emperor ascended and stood on the steps; the Three Elder and Five Senior went out the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elder and Five Senior left; the emperor ascended the steps; they went out the gate.

sentences.zh: 侍中前奏「禮畢」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant advanced and memorialized: "The rites are complete."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported: "The rites are complete."

sentences.zh: 皇帝降，還大次。

translations.literal: The emperor descended and returned to the great waiting station.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended and returned to the great waiting pavilion.

sentences.zh: 三老、五更升安車，導從而還，群官及學生等以次出。

translations.literal: The Three Elder and Five Senior mounted comfort carriages and returned with escort; officials and students exited in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elder and Five Senior rode comfort carriages home with escort; officials and students left in order.

sentences.zh: 明日，三老主旨闕表謝。
